facts.statement: The genus Protitanichthys was first described by Eastman in 1907.
Protitanichthys lived during the Middle Devonian, specifically from the Eifelian to the Lower Givetian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Devonian: Eifelian - Lower Givetian,

facts.statement: Fossils of this animal are found in the Delaware Limestone of Ohio and the Rockport Quarry Limestone of Michigan.
facts.quote: Fossils are found primarily in the Eifelian-epoch aged Delaware Limestone of Ohio, and the Lower Givetian-aged Rockport Quarry Limestone of Michigan

facts.statement: Protitanichthys is an extinct genus of large arthrodire placoderms belonging to the family Coccosteidae.
facts.quote: Protitanichthys is an extinct genus of comparatively large coccosteid arthrodire placoderms

facts.statement: Protitanichthys resembles other coccosteids but has a proportionally narrower skull and smaller eye orbits.
facts.quote: Protitanichthys is very similar to other coccosteids, though the skull is proportionally narrower, and the orbits are comparatively smaller.

facts.statement: Most known specimens of Protitanichthys are about 0.5 meters long, though rare fossils exceed 2 meters.
facts.quote: with most fossil specimens coming from individuals 0.5 m in length, with rare fossils from over 2 m individuals.

facts.statement: Protitanichthys is the second-largest known coccosteid, surpassed only by the genus Livosteus.
facts.quote: It is surpassed only in size by the Old World genus, Livosteus.

facts.statement: The type species Protitanichthys fossatus was described based on a cranial roof approximately 20 cm long found in Ohio.
facts.quote: The description of P. fossatus is based on a cranial roof, possibly 20 cm long, found in the Eifelian-aged Delaware Limestone of Ohio.

facts.statement: Many fragmented remains of the species Protitanichthys rockportensis have been found in Michigan.
facts.quote: As the specific name suggests, numerous scrappy remains of this species are found in the Lower-Givetian Rockport Quarry Limestone in Michigan.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Protitanichthys rockportensis is a distinct species from P. fossatus, as differences are limited to time and location.
facts.quote: Denison (1978) questions the status of P. rockportensis being distinct from P. fossatus, as there are very few differences between the two, aside from chronological and geographical differences.

facts.statement: Protitanichthys belongs to the family Coccosteidae and the clade Coccosteomorphi within Eubrachythoraci.
facts.quote: Protitanichthys is a member of the family Coccosteidae, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database classifies Protitanichthys as a member of the family Panxiosteidae.
Protitanichthys is classified in the class Placodermi.
Protitanichthys lived between 393.47 and 382.31 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Eifelian to Givetian (393.47 to 382.31 million years ago)
